Queue construction¶

Back to Queue API Reference

Signature¶

Queue(const Series& v);
Queue(Series&& v);
Queue(const Note& v);
Queue(Note&& v);
Queue(const Timeline& v);
Queue(Timeline&& v);
Queue(const Duration& v);
Queue(Duration&& v);

What It Does¶

Wraps one payload value – a Series, Note, Timeline, or Duration – in a Queue. There are eight constructors in total: one copying and one moving overload for each of the four payload types. Every one of them is implicit (none is marked explicit), so a Queue can be built directly from a payload expression without naming the constructor, and a function that takes a const Queue& accepts a bare Series/Note/Timeline/ Duration argument too.

Once built, a Queue is not reassignable to a different kind by any public method – the only way to change which payload a Queue holds is to construct a new one.

Parameters¶

v (const Series&, Series&&, const Note&, Note&&, const Timeline&, Timeline&&, const Duration&, or Duration&&)

The payload to wrap. Which overload is selected fixes the new Queue’s kind().

Returns¶

A Queue whose kind() matches the payload type that was passed in.

Examples¶

Example 1. One Queue per payload type, each built from a different public factory. The right-hand side deliberately spells the wrapper as pluss::Queue{payload}: measurements, labels, observed_at, and timeout are plainly the destination variables rather than apparent API names.

const auto measurements = pluss::Queue{pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0})};
const auto labels = pluss::Queue{pluss::make_note({"a", "b"})};
const auto observed_at =
    pluss::Queue{pluss::timeline::make("1999-04-17T21:15:23Z")};
const auto timeout = pluss::Queue{pluss::duration::days(3)};

std::cout << "measurements.kind_name()=" << measurements.kind_name() << '\n';
std::cout << "labels.kind_name()=" << labels.kind_name() << '\n';
std::cout << "observed_at.kind_name()=" << observed_at.kind_name() << '\n';
std::cout << "timeout.kind_name()=" << timeout.kind_name() << '\n';

Output¶

measurements.kind_name()=Series
labels.kind_name()=Note
observed_at.kind_name()=Timeline
timeout.kind_name()=Duration

Each Queue reports the kind of the value it was built from, regardless of which of the four factories produced that value.

Notes¶

  • The constructors are implicit by design: a function parameter typed const Queue& accepts a plain Series, Note, Timeline, or Duration directly, with no explicit wrapping at the call site.

  • Queue has no default constructor. There is no “empty” or “undefined” Queue – every Queue holds exactly one of the four payloads from the moment it is constructed.

See Also¶

  • kind: identifying which payload a Queue holds.

  • accessors: getting the payload back out.
